speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the characteristics of the bleeding from your wisdom tooth extraction site, such as whether it is oozing freely or clotting slowly. Additionally, have you experienced any other bleeding episodes, such as nosebleeds or bleeding gums, unrelated to dental procedures?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the family history of bleeding, joint swelling, and easy bruising in a male patient, do you or your mother notice that his bleeding time is prolonged, and has he ever been told he has a clotting disorder or von Willebrand disease?

REQUEST TEST: PT, PTT, Bleeding Time.
REQUEST IMAGES: CBC with Platelet Count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: PT: 15 sec, PTT: 60 sec, Bleeding Time: 6 min; CBC with Platelet Count: Hematocrit 35%, Leukocyte Count 8,500/mm3, Platelet Count 160,000/mm3

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency).

The prolonged PTT with normal PT and platelet count, combined with the family history of joint swelling and the uncle's similar symptoms, strongly suggests a specific factor deficiency rather than von Willebrand disease. Given your age and the severity of the bleeding, did you experience any spontaneous joint bleeding or hematomas prior to this dental procedure?
